reviewer: heldout_design independent scientific review of saved results
execution_scope: Read saved outcomes, likelihood/macro source, preregistered freeze, committed freeze and forward audit. No fitting, parameter changes, score execution or target-based tuning was performed by this review.

interpretation_findings.finding: The primary R1-minus-conventional plug-in conditional log density is 0.004982690134056611. This is practically negligible here and is not Bayesian model evidence, a Bayes factor, a calibrated significance, or detection of envelope-state response. The tiny change includes separately fitted macro parameters and finite optimizer termination; it is not the fixed-body R1 response.

The conventional primary conditional score exceeds the prescribed zero-delay control by 35.64831676711037 log-density units. This supports timing information in the frozen configured transfer model. The zero-delay control shares the hyperparameters estimated with free delays and is not separately optimized under a null, so this is not a calibrated nested-hypothesis test.

The reported joint score retains temporal/inter-image latent correlations and is correctly the difference of normalized marginalized likelihoods. The sum of marginal predictive log densities is a separate diagnostic. Continuous probability densities in magnitude units can exceed one, so positive log densities are not an error. Scores must be compared in the same units.

These are overlapping factorizations of the same 400 later measurements, not independent replications. The secondary conditional log density equals the driver conditional density plus the primary A/C/D conditional density, as verified from saved likelihood values.

Within each primary score object, the field training_log_likelihood actually denotes the likelihood of the entire conditioning set, historical training plus allowed later B. It is not the historical fitting likelihood and does not imply that later B was used for fitting. The actual conditional-score subtraction is correct.

Conventional primary nominal95% marginal coverage is256/300=85.3333%, with A 62/100, C 99/100 and D 95/100. The observations and intervals are correlated, so these descriptive fractions do not justify an independent-binomial p-value. Intervals are conditional on fitted hyperparameters and macro parameters and omit their uncertainty.

Light-curve offsets absorb constant magnification, extinction and calibration differences, and the model predicts time-delay transfer rather than independently fitting resolved arcs, kinematics, a measured line-of-sight mass distribution or full flux constraints. Mass-profile, optical-screen, source/extrinsic and mass-sheet freedoms remain. The source-derived positive effective-mass representation has exactly the same transfer and score as R1 by construction. These measurements do not select a unique microscopic envelope state.

material_failures_or_unvalidated_require.finding: The shared primary brightness prediction has positive mean residual about 0.07475mag and RMSE about 0.10133mag; imageA alone has bias about +0.11238mag and nominal95% coverage 62%. The free-delay empirical reference also has imageA coverage 63%. Thus most failure is shared by the declared source/extrinsic variability and uncertainty layer rather than evidence for a BHSM-specific response. Do not repair or recenter these targets and call the same experiment held out.

The secondary training-only conventional forecast has RMSE 0.1949449284646148mag and nominal95% coverage 75.5%. Its imageB coverage is 34%, bias about -0.24619mag. This is a weaker, poorly calibrated all-future extrapolation; the current model is not a validated precision forecasting or state-mapping instrument.

A separate forward census finds a fifth central image in both macro models, with predicted macro flux about 6.3% of A. This must be confronted with pixel data, galaxy contamination, extinction, finite-source/microlensing effects and an actual central-image detection limit before full observational admission. Four fitted point-image positions do not supply such a limit. The finite search is not itself proof of a complete R1 image census.

The fitted spherical prescribed Plummer source plus total remote quadratic optical screen is a declared tractable model, not an inferred unique global envelope state. Its screen convergence cannot be identified with an independently measured environmental mass sheet, and no microscopic state-to-geometry closure or complete physical preparation has been established.

forward_audit_review.conclusion: Physical fixed-body response is separately applied with the same ordinary source, body, screen, clock and maps. Refit differences retain nuisance reallocation and finite optimizer effects. Actual source magnification uses (D_os_eff/D_s) times the normalized lens Jacobian. The positive finite effective mass is counted once in the outer-radius bound. These formulas and saved residuals are consistent within the retained approximation.

required_reporting: Publish this as one frozen retrospective observed-lens pilot with a useful transfer comparison and explicit predictive failures. Do not report a unique envelope map, BHSM detection, validated 95% intervals, independent replication, physical admission or acceptance-ready empirical closure. Future changes require a new declared validation target or nested training validation; preserve these outcomes.

local_state_coefficient_map.scope: At fixed lambda the reduced coefficient map alone is not injective in (H,v,d): H remains algebraically free and the sign of v is not selected. These algebraic alternatives are not asserted to solve the complete background or envelope equations. The experiment fixes one adopted background and does not fit b,C or recover a physical state.
